arxiv-2107-10371.title: An In Situ Study of Turbulence Near Stellar Bow Shocks
arxiv-2107-10371.creator: Stella Koch Ocker, James M. Cordes, Shami Chatterjee, Timothy Dolch
arxiv-2107-10371.description: Abstract Stellar bow shocks are observed in a variety of interstellar environments and are shaped by the conditions of gas in the interstellar medium (ISM). In situ measurements of turbulent density fluctuations near stellar bow shocks are only achievable with a few observational probes, including H α \alpha emitting bow shocks and the Voyager Interstellar Mission (VIM) .

arxiv-2111-08995.title: Self-Learning Tuning for Post-Silicon Validation Thanks: This research was supported by Advantest as part of the Graduate School ”Intelligent Methods for Test and Reliability” (GS-IMTR) at the University of Stuttgart.
arxiv-2111-08995.creator: Peter Domanski, Dirk Pflüger, Jochen Rivoir, Raphaël Latty
arxiv-2111-08995.description: Abstract Increasing complexity of modern integrated circuits makes design validation more difficult. Existing approaches are not able anymore to cope with the complexity of tasks such as robust performance tuning in post-silicon validation. Therefore, we propose a novel learn-to-optimize approach based on reinforcement learning in order to solve complex and mixed-type tuning tasks in an efficient and robust way.

arxiv-2303-12847.title: Scalar decay into pions via Higgs portal
arxiv-2303-12847.creator: Dmitry Gorbunov, Ekaterina Kriukova, Oleg Teryaev
arxiv-2303-12847.description: Abstract In extensions of the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics a light scalar from a hidden sector can interact with known particles via mixing with the SM Higgs boson. If the scalar mass is of GeV scale, this coupling induces the scalar decay into light hadrons, that saturates the scalar width.

arxiv-2306-09499.title: From unbiased to maximal entropy random walks on hypergraphs
arxiv-2306-09499.creator: Pietro Traversa, Guilherme Ferraz de Arruda, Yamir Moreno
arxiv-2306-09499.description: Abstract Random walks have been intensively studied on regular and complex networks, which are used to represent pairwise interactions. Nonetheless, recent works have demonstrated that many real-world processes are better captured by higher-order relationships, which are naturally represented by hypergraphs. Here, we study random walks on hypergraphs.

arxiv-2310-02275.title: MuSe-GNN: Learning Unified Gene Representation From Multimodal Biological Graph Data
arxiv-2310-02275.creator: Tianyu Liu, Yuge Wang, Rex Ying, Hongyu Zhao*
arxiv-2310-02275.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tianyu Liu, Yuge Wang, Rex Ying, Hongyu Zhao*. Discovering genes with similar functions across diverse biomedical contexts poses a significant challenge in gene representation learning due to data heterogeneity. In this study, we resolve this problem by introducing a novel model called Multimodal Similarity Learning Graph Neural Network, which combines Multimodal Machine Learning and Deep Graph Neural Networks to learn gene representations from single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data.

arxiv-2311-17643.title: Thera: Aliasing-Free Arbitrary-Scale Super-Resolution with Neural Heat Fields
arxiv-2311-17643.creator: Alexander Becker, Rodrigo Caye Daudt, Dominik Narnhofer, Torben Peters, Nando Metzger, Jan Dirk Wegner, Konrad Schindler
arxiv-2311-17643.description: Abstract Recent approaches to arbitrary-scale single image super-resolution (ASR) use neural fields to represent continuous signals that can be sampled at arbitrary resolutions. However, point-wise queries of neural fields do not naturally match the point spread function (PSF) of pixels, which may cause aliasing in the super-resolved image.

arxiv-2407-07998.title: What’s the score? Automated Denoising Score Matching for Nonlinear Diffusions
arxiv-2407-07998.creator: Raghav Singhal, Mark Goldstein, Rajesh Ranganath
arxiv-2407-07998.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Raghav Singhal, Mark Goldstein, Rajesh Ranganath. Reversing a diffusion process by learning its score forms the heart of diffusion-based generative modeling and for estimating properties of scientific systems. The diffusion processes that are tractable center on linear processes with a Gaussian stationary distribution. This limits the kinds of models that can be built to those that target a Gaussian prior or more generally limits the kinds of problems that can be generically solved to those that have conditionally linear score functions.

arxiv-2409-07189.title: AI-Guided Molecular Simulations in VR: Exploring Strategies for Imitation Learning in Hyperdimensional Molecular Systems
arxiv-2409-07189.creator: Mohamed Dhouioui, Jonathan Barnoud, Rhoslyn Roebuck Williams, Harry J. Stroud, Phil Bates, David R. Glowacki
arxiv-2409-07189.description: Abstract Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are a crucial computational tool for researchers to understand and engineer molecular structure and function in areas such as drug discovery, protein engineering, and material design. Despite their utility, MD simulations are expensive, owing to the high dimensionality of molecular systems.

arxiv-2504-02278.title: Digital-twin imaging based on descattering Gaussian splatting Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2504-02278.creator: Suguru Shimomura, * Kazuki Yamanouchi, and Jun Tanida
arxiv-2504-02278.description: Abstract Three-dimensional imaging through scattering media is important in medical science and astronomy. We propose a digital-twin imaging method based on Gaussian splatting to observe an object behind a scattering medium. A digital twin model built through data assimilation, emulates the behavior of objects and environmental changes in a virtual space.

arxiv-2506-00780.title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
arxiv-2506-00780.creator: Jingyu Liu, Jingquan Peng, Xiaopeng Wu, Xubing Li, Tiezheng Ge, Bo Zheng, Yong Liu
arxiv-2506-00780.description: Abstract Despite the widespread application of Large Language Models (LLMs) across various domains, they frequently exhibit overconfidence when encountering uncertain scenarios, yet existing solutions primarily rely on evasive responses (e.g., "I don’t know") overlooks the opportunity of identifying and addressing the uncertainty to generate more satisfactory responses.

arxiv-2507-06480.title: Periodic Korteweg-de Vries soliton potentials generate quasisymmetric magnetic field strength in a finite plasma- β \beta equilibrium
arxiv-2507-06480.creator: W. Sengupta, R. Madan, S. Buller, N. Nikulsin, E.J. Paul, R. Nies, A.A. Kaptanoglu, S.R. Hudson, A. Bhattacharjee
arxiv-2507-06480.description: Abstract Quasisymmetry (QS) is a hidden symmetry of the magnetic field strength, B B , that enables effective confinement of charged particles in a fully three-dimensional (3D) toroidal plasma equilibrium. Such equilibria are typically modeled by the ideal magnetohydrostatic (MHS) equation.

arxiv-2511-07125.title: Towards a Rigorous Understanding of the Population Dynamics of the NSGA-III: Tight Runtime Bounds
arxiv-2511-07125.creator: Andre Opris
arxiv-2511-07125.description: Abstract Evolutionary algorithms are widely used for solving multi-objective optimization problems. A prominent example is NSGA-III, which is particularly well suited for solving problems involving more than three objectives, distinguishing it from the classical NSGA-II. Despite its empirical success, the theoretical understanding of NSGA III remains very limited, especially with respect to runtime analysis.

arxiv-2512-10470.title: Stealth and Evasion in Rogue AP Attacks: An Analysis of Modern Detection and Bypass Techniques
arxiv-2512-10470.creator: Kaleb Bacztub, Braden Vester, Matteo Hodge, Liulseged Abate
arxiv-2512-10470.description: Abstract Wireless networks act as the backbone of modern digital connectivity, making them a primary target for cyber adversaries. Rogue Access Point (AP) attacks, specifically the “Evil Twin” variant, enable attackers to clone legitimate wireless network identifiers to deceive users into connecting. Once a connection is established, the adversary can intercept traffic and harvest sensitive credentials.

pmc-10717449.title: COVID-19- related work, managerial factors and exhaustion among general practitioners in Sweden: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10717449.creator: Helena Månsson Sandberg, Bodil J Landstad, Åsa Tjulin, Emma Brulin
pmc-10717449.description: IntroductionA significant number of international studies show that general practitioners (GPs) suffered from burnout when working during the COVID-19 pandemic. A Swedish study found that more than 16% of GPs had exhaustion in spring 2021. Exhaustion can be regarded as an initial stage of burnout.

pmc-11361636.title: Conjugation of ATG8s to single membranes at a glance
pmc-11361636.creator: Carmen Figueras-Novoa, Lewis Timimi, Elena Marcassa, Rachel Ulferts, Rupert Beale
pmc-11361636.description: Autophagy refers to a set of degradative mechanisms whereby cytoplasmic contents are targeted to the lysosome. This is best described for macroautophagy, where a double-membrane compartment (autophagosome) is generated to engulf cytoplasmic contents. Autophagosomes are decorated with ubiquitin-like ATG8 molecules (ATG8s), which are recruited through covalent lipidation, catalysed by the E3-ligase-like ATG16L1 complex.

pmc-11472633.title: Healthcare resource utilisation and costs in infants with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infections: a national population cohort study
pmc-11472633.creator: Hyun Jin Han, Dahye Ryu, Ju Young Kim, Semin Jang, Hae Sun Suh
pmc-11472633.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of severe respiratory infections in infants worldwide, significantly affecting their health and contributing to the global healthcare burden. We aimed to examine healthcare resource utilisation patterns and costs for infants under one year old with confirmed RSV infection across subgroups of different gestational ages and health conditions and the cost implications of RSV infections over time, thereby demonstrating the economic burden of the disease.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study utilised nationwide claims data from the Korea

pmc-11645941.title: P040 How do Children with Neurodisability Use Technology Around Bedtime? Results from a Cross-Sectional Survey
pmc-11645941.creator: I Shin, M Anderson, J Robinson, M Vandeleur, K Waters, J Chawla
pmc-11645941.description: IntroductionAnecdotally caregivers of children with neurodisability (ND) express that using an electronic device before bed helps to calm their child and prepare them for sleep. The aim of this study was to determine how children with ND use technology prior to bedtime.

pmc-11659085.title: The family alliance as a facilitator of therapeutic change in systemic relational psychotherapy for borderline personality disorder: A case study
pmc-11659085.creator: Iolanda D'Ascenzo, Anna Vilaregut, Verónica Zurdo, Sonia Torras, Ignacio Bolaños Cartujo
pmc-11659085.description: Managing the Therapeutic Alliance is often complex when it comes to the treatment of borderline personality disorder (BPD), but the alliance is crucial for the success of the therapy. Combined individual and family interventions have been shown to be very useful in treating of these cases. This study has two objectives.

pmc-11710746.title: Epigenomics and single cell CRISPR screening to investigate the risk‐modifying role of microglia in Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis
pmc-11710746.creator: Michael D Gallagher, Wenjuan Du, Katheryn EA Hazel, Zeynep Aydin, Yiran Cheng, Bingbing Yuan, George W Bell, Richard A Young, Rudolf Jaenisch, Olivia Corradin
pmc-11710746.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) cause substantial health‐related and economic burdens, but progress towards preventative or ameliorative treatments has been limited. Genome‐wide association studies have identified hundreds of risk loci containing single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that alter risk for these diseases, but >90% of these SNPs are in noncoding regions, which are cell type‐specific and difficult to study.

pmc-13216114.title: Trends and Outcomes in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Surgery: A Nationwide Analysis of Improvements From 2010 to 2022
pmc-13216114.creator: Maya S Abu-Zahra, William J Karakash, Daniel Rusu, Justin W Zheng, Aidan Lindgren, Chimere O Ezuma, Henry Avetisian, Jeffrey C Wang, Ram K Alluri, Raymond J Hah, Michael M Safaee
pmc-13216114.description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo evaluate national trends in management and outcomes of posterior spinal fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) over a 12-year period and characterize postoperative opioid utilization.MethodsWe used the PearlDiver Mariner database to identify patients aged 10-18 years with AIS undergoing posterior spinal fusion of >7 levels from 2010-2022.

pmc-13249161.title: Advancing Lipid Management: Saudi Heart Association Position Statement on PCSK9-targeted Therapies in the Primary and Secondary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease
pmc-13249161.creator: Waleed AlHabeeb, Hussein Alamri, Hussein Elbadawi, Yazed S AlRuthia, Waleed Alharbi, Owayed Alshammeri, Adel Tash, Shadi Almoziny, Naji Kholaif, Hussain Halawani, Fadia AlMahdi, Wael Yar, Khalid F Alhabib
pmc-13249161.description: BackgroundDespite robust evidence for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prevention, attainment of guideline-recommended targets remains suboptimal in Saudi Arabia, especially among high- and very high-risk patients. Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type 9 (PCSK9)-targeted therapies, which include monoclonal antibodies (evolocumab, alirocumab) and small interfering RNA (inclisiran), offer potent LDL-C lowering that can help address this gap.

pmc-13280315.title: Ramucirumab induces apoptosis in Caco-2 cells via mitochondrial impairment and caspase activation
pmc-13280315.creator: Amal M Al-Dogmi, Khalid Mashay Al-Anazi, Wajhul Qamar, Mohammad Abul Farah

pmc-13639009.title: Characteristic spatiotemporal features of large-scale functional network architecture in posttraumatic stress disorder
pmc-13639009.creator: Jianze Wu, Zhen Cai, Leah J. Hudson, Wenkun Lei, Feng Chen, Guangming Lu, Yuan Zhong
pmc-13639009.description: Understanding how trauma reshapes the brain’s large-scale functional architecture requires a framework that integrates both spatial and temporal dimensions. In this study, we applied a multimodal analytic framework that combines functional connectivity gradient mapping with energy landscape analysis. This approach allowed us to characterize cortical reconfiguration in trauma-exposed controls (TEC) and individuals with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

uslaw-usc-t42-s1383d.title: 42 U.S.C. § 1383d — Outreach program for children
uslaw-usc-t42-s1383d.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s1383d.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 7 (Social Security); Subchapter XVI (Supplemental Security Income For Aged, Blind, And Disabled); Part B (Procedural And General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Establishment The Commissioner of Social Security shall establish and conduct an ongoing program of outreach to children who are potentially eligible for benefits under this subchapter.

uslaw-usc-t42-s7144a.title: 42 U.S.C. § 7144a — Establishment of security, counterintelligence, and intelligence policies
uslaw-usc-t42-s7144a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s7144a.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 84 (Department Of Energy); Subchapter II (Establishment Of Department). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary shall be responsible for developing and promulgating the security, counterintelligence, and intelligence policies of the Department. The Secretary may use the immediate staff of the Secretary to assist in developing and promulgating those policies.
